items.title: Smell, Counted One Through Ten Ways

items.zh: 或立一種香。謂由鼻所行義故。或立二種。謂內及外。或立三種。謂可意、不可意、及處中香。
items.en: Or smell may be established as one kind: that which the nose operates upon. Or it may be established as two kinds: internal, and external. Or it may be established as three kinds: pleasant, unpleasant, and neutral.

items.zh: 或立四種。謂四大香。一、沈香，二、窣堵魯迦香，三、龍腦香，四、麝香。或立五種。謂根香、莖香、葉香、花香、果香。
items.en: Or it may be established as four kinds, the four great fragrances: agarwood, storax, camphor, and musk. Or it may be established as five kinds: the fragrance of roots, of stems, of leaves, of flowers, and of fruit.

items.zh: 或立六種。謂食香、飲香、衣香、莊嚴具香、乘香、宮室香。或立七種。謂皮香、葉香、素泣謎羅香、栴檀香、三辛香、熏香、末香。
items.en: Or it may be established as six kinds: the fragrance of food, of drink, of clothing, of ornament, of a conveyance, and of a dwelling. Or it may be established as seven kinds: the fragrance of bark, of leaves, a certain red Indian fragrance, sandalwood, the three pungent spices, incense, and powdered fragrance.

items.zh: 或立八種。謂俱生香、非俱生香、恒續香、非恒續香、雜香、純香、猛香、非猛香。或立九種。謂過去、未來、現在等，如前說。
items.en: Or it may be established as eight kinds: innate fragrance, acquired fragrance, continuously enduring fragrance, not continuously enduring fragrance, mixed fragrance, pure fragrance, intense fragrance, and mild fragrance. Or it may be established as nine kinds: past, future, present, and so on, as already explained.

items.zh: 或立十種。謂女香、男香、一指香、二指香、唾香、洟香、脂髓膿血香、肉香、雜糅香、淤埿香。
items.en: Or it may be established as ten kinds: the fragrance of a woman, of a man, the length of one finger, the length of two fingers, of saliva, of nasal mucus, of fat and marrow and pus and blood, of flesh, of a mixture, and of mire.

items.zh: 或立一種味。謂由舌所行義故。或立二種。謂內及外。或立三種。謂可意等如前說。或立四種。謂大麥味、粳稻味、小麥味、餘下穀味。或立五種。謂酒飲味、非酒飲味、蔬菜味、林果味、所食味。
items.en: It may be established as one kind of taste, because it is what the tongue ranges over. Or as two kinds: inner and outer. Or as three kinds: agreeable and so on, as explained before. Or as four kinds: the taste of barley, of rice, of wheat, and of the other lesser grains. Or as five kinds: the taste of alcoholic drinks, of non-alcoholic drinks, of vegetables, of forest fruits, and of cooked food.

items.title: Taste, Counted Six Through Ten Ways

items.zh: 或立六種。謂甘苦等。或立七種。謂酥味、油味、蜜味、甘蔗變味、乳酪味、鹽味、肉味。
items.en: Or it may be established as six kinds: sweet, bitter, and so on. Or it may be established as seven kinds: the taste of ghee, of oil, of honey, of refined sugarcane, of curdled milk, of salt, and of meat.

items.zh: 或立八種。如香說。或立九種。亦如香說。
items.en: Or it may be established as eight kinds, as already explained for smell. Or it may be established as nine kinds, likewise as already explained for smell.

items.zh: 或立十種。謂可嚼味、可噉味、可甞味、可飲味、可吮味、可爆乾味、充足味、休愈味、盪滌味、常習味。後五謂諸藥味。
items.en: Or it may be established as ten kinds: the chewable, the swallowable, the tasteable, the drinkable, the suckable, the dryable, the fortifying, the curative, the cleansing, and the habitually taken. The last five of these are the tastes of medicines.

items.title: Touch, Counted One Through Ten Ways

items.zh: 或立一種觸。謂由身所行義故。或立二種。如香說。或立三種。謂可意等。或立四種。謂摩觸、搦觸、打觸、揉觸。
items.en: Or touch may be established as one kind: that which the body operates upon. Or it may be established as two kinds, as already explained for smell. Or it may be established as three kinds: pleasant, and so on. Or it may be established as four kinds: rubbing, pressing, striking, and kneading.

items.zh: 或立五種。謂五趣差別。又有五種。謂蚊䗈風日蛇蠍等觸。或立六種。謂苦、樂、不苦不樂、俱生、所治攝、能治攝。
items.en: Or it may be established as five kinds, according to differences among the five destinies. Or, again, as five kinds: the touch of a mosquito, a gnat, a flea, a louse, a snake, or a scorpion. Or it may be established as six kinds: painful, pleasant, neither painful nor pleasant, innate, that requiring treatment, and that which treats.

items.zh: 或立七種。謂堅鞕觸、流濕觸、煖觸、動觸、跳墮觸、摩按觸、身變異觸。謂濕滑等。或立八種。謂手觸觸、塊觸觸、杖觸觸、刀觸觸、冷觸觸、煖觸觸、飢觸觸、渴觸觸。
items.en: Or it may be established as seven kinds: hard touch, flowing-moist touch, warm touch, moving touch, the touch of jumping or falling, rubbing touch, and the touch of bodily change — that is, dampness, smoothness, and the like. Or it may be established as eight kinds: the touch of a hand, of a clod, of a staff, of a blade, cold touch, warm touch, the touch of hunger, and the touch of thirst.

items.zh: 或立九種。如香說。或立十種。謂食觸、飲觸、乘觸、衣觸、莊嚴具觸、床坐觸、机橙臺枕及方座觸、女觸、男觸、彼二相事受用觸。
items.en: Or it may be established as nine kinds, as already explained for smell. Or it may be established as ten kinds: the touch of eating, of drinking, of riding, of clothing, of ornament, of bed and seat, of stool, stand, pillow, and square seat, the touch of a woman, the touch of a man, and the touch of the two sexes' mutual enjoyment.

items.title: The Sixth Object: Dharmas, Eighty-Seven in All

items.zh: 略說法界，若假若實，有八十七法。彼復云何？謂心所有法有五十三，始從作意，乃至尋、伺為後邊。
items.en: Briefly stated, the sphere of dharmas — whether conceptually existent or substantially real — comprises eighty-seven dharmas. What are these? Mental factors number fifty-three, beginning with attention and ending with investigation and analysis.

items.zh: 法處所攝色有二種。謂律儀不律儀所攝色、三摩地所行色。
items.en: Form comprised within the sphere of dharmas is of two kinds: form comprised in formal precepts and their absence, and form that operates within meditative absorption.

items.title: The Twenty-Four Forces Dissociated from Mind

items.zh: 不相應行有二十四種，謂得、無想定、滅盡定、無想異熟、命根、眾同分、異生性、生、老、住、無常、名身、句身、文身、流轉、定異、相應、勢速、次第、時、方、數、和合、不和合。
items.en: Forces dissociated from mind number twenty-four: acquisition; the attainment of no-perception; the attainment of cessation; the karmic ripening of no-perception; the life-faculty; a shared class among beings; the ordinary being's own nature; arising; ageing; abiding; impermanence; a body of names; a body of phrases; a body of syllables; flux; fixed distinction; correspondence; swiftness; sequence; time; direction; number; concordance; and discordance.

items.zh: 無為有八事。謂虛空、非擇滅、擇滅、善、不善、無記法真如、不動、想受滅。
items.en: The unconditioned comprises eight things: space; cessation not through discernment; cessation through discernment; the true nature of wholesome dharmas, of unwholesome dharmas, and of indeterminate dharmas; the unmoving; and the cessation of ideation and feeling.

items.title: Eight or Six — Same Thing, Different Count

items.zh: 如是無為，廣八略六，若六若八，平等平等。
items.en: Thus the unconditioned, spoken of fully, is eight; spoken of briefly, is six. Whether counted as six or as eight, they are exactly equivalent.

items.title: The Sphere of Dharmas Itself, Counted One Through Nine Ways

items.zh: 復次，法界或立一種。謂由意所行義。或立二種。謂假所攝法、非假所攝法。
items.en: Further, the sphere of dharmas may be established as one kind: that which mental consciousness operates upon. Or it may be established as two kinds: dharmas comprised as conceptually existent, and dharmas comprised as not conceptually existent.

items.zh: 或立三種。謂有色、無色、及有為無為。或立四種。謂有色假所攝法、無色心所有所攝法、無色不相應假所攝法、無色無為假非假所攝法。
items.en: Or it may be established as three kinds: possessing form, formless, and unconditioned. Or it may be established as four kinds: form comprised as conceptually existent, the formless comprised as mental factors, the formless comprised as conceptually existent dissociated forces, and the formless unconditioned comprised as both conceptually existent and not.

items.zh: 或立五種。謂色、心所法、心不相應行、善、無記無為。或立六種。謂受、想、相應行、不相應行、色、無為。
items.en: Or it may be established as five kinds: form, mental factors, forces dissociated from mind, wholesome unconditioned, and indeterminate unconditioned. Or it may be established as six kinds: feeling, ideation, associated formations, dissociated formations, form, and the unconditioned.

items.zh: 或立七種。謂受、想、思、染污、不染污、色、無為。或立八種。謂善、不善、無記、受、想、行、色、無為。
items.en: Or it may be established as seven kinds: feeling, ideation, volition, the defiled, the undefiled, form, and the unconditioned. Or it may be established as eight kinds: wholesome, unwholesome, indeterminate, feeling, ideation, formations, form, and the unconditioned.

items.zh: 或立九種。謂由過去、未來等差別。
items.en: Or it may be established as nine kinds, according to differences of past, future, and the rest.

items.zh: 或立十種。謂由十種義。一、隨逐生義；二、領所緣義；三、取所緣相義；四、於所緣造作義；五、即彼諸法分位差別義；六、無障礙義；七、常離繫義；八、常非離繫義；九、常無顛倒義；十、苦樂離繫義、非受離繫義及受離繫義。
items.en: Or it may be established as ten kinds, by ten distinct meanings: first, the meaning of following mind's arising; second, the meaning of receiving what is taken as object; third, the meaning of grasping the mark of what is taken as object; fourth, the meaning of acting upon what is taken as object; fifth, the meaning of the differing momentary phases of these very dharmas; sixth, the meaning of being unobstructed; seventh, the meaning of being permanently free of bondage; eighth, the meaning of being permanently other than free of bondage; ninth, the meaning of being permanently free of distortion; tenth, the meaning of freedom from bondage to pleasure and pain, freedom from bondage that involves no feeling, and freedom from bondage that involves feeling.

blocks.text: The counting continues through smell, taste, and touch, then reaches the sixth object, the "sphere of dharmas" (法界), which only the mental consciousness knows. Here the treatise lists eighty-seven dharmas, and this list is the direct ancestor of the *Hundred Dharmas*. If you know the Hundred Dharmas Map, you will recognise almost everything.

One passage is missing from Ru-Yi's translation (now supplied in our own translation, marked as ours) (0293b11–b15): taste as one kind (what the tongue operates on), two (inner and outer), three (agreeable and so on), four (the tastes of barley, rice, wheat, and other grains), and five (of alcoholic drinks, non-alcoholic drinks, vegetables, and so on).

Smell is counted up to ten ways. The four great fragrances are agarwood, storax, camphor, and musk. Among the ten are "one-finger" and "two-finger" fragrance; Master Cháng Bǎi's lecture explains these as incense one or two fingers long. The point of such lists is concreteness: the treatise wants the meditator to recognise the ordinary objects of experience precisely.

Ten kinds: the chewable, the swallowable, the tasteable, the drinkable, the suckable, and five that "are the tastes of medicines": the dryable, the fortifying, the curative, the cleansing, and the habitually taken.

Eight kinds by cause: the touch of a hand, a clod, a staff, a blade, cold, warmth, hunger, and thirst. Six kinds include touch "requiring treatment" and touch "that treats", which Master Cháng Bǎi explains as the feeling of being ill and the touch of taking medicine or bathing.
The objects only the mental consciousness knows add up to eighty-seven:

items: **Two kinds of form in the sphere of dharmas** (法處所攝色): the form of precepts and their absence, and form produced in meditation. Both teachers: the first is conceptual (the "precept-body" is a firm resolve, not matter); only meditation-produced form is real.

**Twenty-four formations dissociated from mind** (心不相應行), such as acquisition, the two attainments without mind, the life-faculty, birth, ageing, abiding, impermanence, names, phrases, syllables, time, direction, number, and so on. All are conceptual: labels set up on the phases of matter and mind.

blocks.text: Venerable Miào Jìng does the arithmetic: 53 + 2 + 24 + 8 = 87.

Space; **cessation through discernment** (擇滅), which is nirvāṇa, reached by wisdom; **cessation not through discernment** (非擇滅), which happens only because conditions are lacking; the unmoving; the cessation of perception and feeling; and the suchness of wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate dharmas.

The two cessations are worth comparing. Master Cháng Bǎi: if I stop speaking, that stopping did not come from wisdom, only from conditions lacking. Venerable Miào Jìng: death is a cessation too, but brings no liberation. Only cessation through discernment frees. Both teachers identify "the unmoving" with the fourth dhyāna, free of eight disturbances (investigation, analysis, in-breath, out-breath, joy, pleasure, grief, pain) and untouched by the three calamities of Day 9.
"Eight in full, six in brief." Fold the three suchnesses into one and the eight become the six of the *Hundred Dharmas*.

The sphere of dharmas is two kinds: conceptually existent and not. Further counts follow, up to ten, with ten meanings behind them. Venerable Miào Jìng's example for suchness as "permanently free of distortion": if someone strikes you with the meditation stick and anger arises ("you look down on me"), that is distortion; taken as part of the path, the same blow brings joy.

quiz.q: When smell is established as four kinds, what are "the four great fragrances"?
options: root, stem, leaf, and flower fragrance
the fragrances of precepts, concentration, wisdom, liberation
quiz.why: "The four great fragrances: agarwood, storax, camphor, and musk." A gives four of the five plant fragrances; C is the familiar "fragrance of precepts, concentration …" — Venerable Miào Jìng noted in Q&A that the treatise does not mention it here, though other texts do. Master Cháng Bǎi: agarwood is dense and dark and sinks in water.

quiz.q: When touch is established as eight kinds, what are they?
options: rubbing, pressing, striking, kneading, cold, warm, smooth, rough
painful, pleasant, neutral, innate, to be treated, treating, male, female
earth, water, fire, wind, light, heavy, smooth, rough
the touch of a hand, a clod, a staff, a blade, cold, warmth, hunger, and thirst
quiz.why: "The touch of a hand, of a clod, of a staff, of a blade, cold touch, warm touch, the touch of hunger, and the touch of thirst" — touch sorted by its cause. Venerable Miào Jìng: 觸觸 is doubled because there is that which touches and that which is touched; Master Cháng Bǎi: hunger and thirst count as touch, which is notable. A mixes in the four kinds (rubbing, pressing, striking, kneading).

quiz.q: The treatise says the sphere of dharmas, conceptual and real, comprises eighty-seven. How is that number made up?
options: fifty-three mental factors + two kinds of dharma-sphere form + twenty-four dissociated forces + eight unconditioned
quiz.why: The text lists in turn: fifty-three mental factors (§60), two kinds of form in the sphere of dharmas (§61), twenty-four dissociated forces (§62), and eight unconditioned (§63). Venerable Miào Jìng works it out: 53 + 2 = 55, plus 24 is 79, plus 8 "makes exactly eighty-seven." Note that the sphere of dharmas excludes mind itself (which belongs to the mind-base), so B is wrong.

quiz.q: Form in the sphere of dharmas is of two kinds: that comprised in precepts and their absence, and that operating in absorption. Which do both teachers say is conceptual and which real?
options: the form of precepts and their absence (the precept-body, or form arising from taking a vow) is conceptual; the form operating in absorption (produced by meditative mastery) is real
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Precept and non-precept form is also conceptual; only absorption-form is real, with real substance." Master Cháng Bǎi: "Precept and non-precept form means the good and bad precept-body, also called form arising from a vow — conceptual form; absorption-form is form manifested by great meditative power — real form." C reverses them.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT among the twenty-four forces dissociated from mind?
quiz.why: Attention is one of the five universal mental factors, in the category of mind and mental factors — not a dissociated force. The twenty-four are: acquisition, the attainment of no-perception, the attainment of cessation, the ripening of no-perception, the life-faculty, shared class, the ordinary being's nature, arising, ageing, abiding, impermanence, bodies of names, phrases, and syllables, flux, fixed distinction, correspondence, swiftness, sequence, time, direction, number, concordance, and discordance. Venerable Miào Jìng: "These twenty-four dissociated forces are all conceptual; none is a real dharma." Master Cháng Bǎi: shared class is what humans have in common with one another, which a human and a dog do not.

quiz.q: What is "cessation not through discernment" among the eight unconditioned, and what examples do the teachers give?
options: ceasing without any discernment, only for lack of conditions — like speech that stops, or a sound that dies in an instant; death too is a ceasing, but brings no liberation
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Say I'm speaking now and then stop — that stopping did not come from wisdom's discernment, only from the conditions lacking." Venerable Miào Jìng: "When this body dies, that is a ceasing — but without liberation. Cessation through discernment, that is liberation"; and a sound ceasing in an instant "has entered nirvāṇa," while we remain beings in saṃsāra. A and B describe cessation *through* discernment.

quiz.q: The treatise says the unconditioned is "eight in full, six in brief — exactly equivalent." How do eight become six?
options: by dropping space and cessation of ideation and feeling
by folding the suchness of wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate dharmas into a single "suchness"
by merging the unmoving and the cessation of ideation and feeling
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Make the suchness of wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate dharmas into one, and in total there are six." Master Cháng Bǎi: the *Hundred Dharmas* treatise counts six; this treatise separates the three suchnesses to make eight — no difference in substance. Venerable Miào Jìng adds that only the three suchnesses are real; the other five unconditioned are provisionally designated.
